name: Online safety · firm stress test
evidenceNote: Limited historical evidence pack prepared 5 September 2026. Summaries describe the dated publications, not an exhaustive statement of current law. Synthetic assets deliberately contain test assumptions. Law-team verification of interpretation and applicability is required before presentation. No research occurs at runtime.

development.title: Ofcom scrutiny of documented illegal-harms risk assessments
development.summary: Ofcom's March 2025 publication describes illegal-content risk assessments and written records for services in scope of the UK's Online Safety Act. Test a hypothetical Singapore obligation using this comparator.

sources.title: Scrutinising illegal harms risk assessments
sources.relevantText: Ofcom's 3 March 2025 publication explains that providers in scope must assess illegal-content risks and retain written records of the assessment process and findings. Selected services were asked to submit records by 31 March. Scope and procedural details must be checked against the underlying Act and guidance; this publication does not establish Singapore duties.

sources.title: IMDA's Online Safety Code comes into effect
sources.relevantText: IMDA's July 2023 announcement describes an Online Safety Code taking effect on 18 July 2023, requiring designated social media services to enhance online safety and curb harmful content. The designated-service approach is a comparator for the hypothetical scope. This limited summary does not establish the absence of any existing Singapore risk-assessment obligation.

firmAssets.title: Online Safety Compliance Playbook
assumptions: Synthetic operating policy: a designated social-media client can complete onboarding without a documented illegal-content risk assessment.

sections.text: For designated social-media platform clients, close the online-safety onboarding review once the content-reporting contact is recorded. Do not request or retain a written illegal-content risk assessment as part of this workflow.

Confirm the designated social-media client's reporting contact and mark online-safety onboarding complete. Evidence required: contact name and email only; no risk-assessment document or retention check is required.

firmAssets.title: Associate Training / Internal Guidance
assumptions: The training procedure delegates its substantive requirements to the current checklist.

sections.text: Use the Platform Client Compliance Checklist, Step 6, to teach completion of online-safety onboarding. The facilitator's exercise and answer key follow that step. Refresh both whenever the checklist changes.

firmAssets.title: Template Client Advisory
assumptions: Recipients include designated and non-designated services; designation has not been verified for every recipient.

sections.text: Our platform client mailing list includes both designated social-media services and other online services. This template summarises the firm's onboarding approach by reference to Playbook 4.2. Before issuing an update, the responsible partner must determine which recipients fall within the relevant obligation.

firmAssets.title: Standard Contract / Platform Clause Set
assumptions: This excerpt addresses payment only and does not allocate online-safety duties.

sections.text: The client shall pay the agreed professional fees within thirty days of receipt of invoice. Any change to the fee schedule requires written agreement by both parties.
